why: Nine Ciutat Vella / Eixample lanes, none placeable: no street plaque, no landmark (#2 and #6 inspected at 2000 px: a pharmacy cross, an arcade, nothing that names the street). The old h-contract died for the same reason; p4 stays typographic on its red field.

place: Passeig de Gràcia at Carrer de Provença, Barcelona — the city's pedestrian wayfinding post in front of La Pedrera (Casa Milà)
how_known: Read at 2000 px: blades 'C. de Provença' and 'Sagrada Família' (arrows right), the post listing 'Pl. de Catalunya', 'Passeig de Gràcia' (L3 and R markers), 'Fundació Antoni Tàpies', 'Casa Batlló', 'Casa Amatller', 'Casa Lleó Morera'; behind, out of focus, La Pedrera's undulating stone façade with its wrought-iron seaweed balconies, which stands at exactly that corner.
caption_proposed: Passeig de Gràcia at Provença, La Pedrera behind: the street points to every door; the Book has already said which.
corners: TL: the wayfinding post's blades, 'Pl. de Catalunya' / 'Passeig de Gràcia' with L3 and R markers — municipal signage that is the frame's subject, not a brand; TR: La Pedrera façade, window and balcony (blurred); BL: the black sign pole and post; BR: La Pedrera balcony ironwork — no logo, wordmark or watermark
ai_signs: none — lettering correct and consistent (Provença with cedilla, Família accented, Lleó Morera), real lens blur on the façade
why: True and clean, and it carries the chapter's habit: on the day the street offers every Gaudí door at once, and the reader arrives with the call already made (the Gaudí Fork, Batlló or La Pedrera). La Pedrera is printed nowhere else; the 2+1 poster carries Batlló. At 816×740 the window is the left 73.5 % of the frame, which keeps both blades and their arrows whole (they end at x≈0.65). 6151 px native over 816 px is 5.5×.

The good frames are La Boqueria (#3, #9: gate and coat of arms), but the Boqueria is not in the book — the Ground's close is about the four charges and the transit costume, and a market gate would need a caption the text does not support. The stall close-ups (#1, #4, #6-#8) carry price cards and stall names in the corners, the fault that killed p-ground. Typographic.

place: Barceloneta beach seen from the water on an overcast day, Barcelona — the sail-shaped hotel at the harbour mouth, the Torre de Sant Sebastià cable-car tower, Montjuïc with the Torre de Jaume I behind
how_known: Read at 6000 px: the sail-shaped glass tower at the harbour mouth (the W, its 'W' a smudge at that size and illegible at print), the lattice cable-car tower of Sant Sebastià on the Barceloneta shore, the Montjuïc ridge with the port cable car's Torre de Jaume I and a Ferris wheel before it, the palm-lined Passeig Marítim and the beach curving away to the right. Only Barcelona has that combination.
caption_proposed: Barceloneta on a gray day, the sand nearly empty: the sea out of play, the city behind it intact.
corners: TL: overcast sky; TR: overcast sky; BL: open water; BR: open water — no mark, logo, text or watermark
ai_signs: none — phone-camera smearing in the fine detail at 100 % (real sensor processing), architecture consistent and correctly placed
why: The chapter's own words — 'whether the sea is in play' — made visible: a beach under cloud, almost empty, the waterfront city lit and whole. The caption claims a gray day, not a month, since the season cannot be read. Not a golden frame: the low light falls on the shore, but the sun is not visible and the sky is gray, not orange (the Bunkers keeps the one golden slot). A different beach and subject from the Poblenou closing on p56 (Barceloneta, not Bogatell–Mar Bella; the Mapfre towers are not in it). 12000 px native; the window keeps the whole coast band (x 0.26–1.0) and cuts only open water on the left.

Mostly not Barcelona (family portraits, statues, a figurine). The two true frames are Sagrada Família: #9 the nave vault (the same subject as the A04 interior square on the 2+1 poster, so one subject, one picture) and #3 the Passion façade shot into the sun (a visible sun flare, and the same basilica). Typographic.

'HOTEL' must name what the frame shows. The apartment façades (#2, #6, #7, #9) would put HOTEL over apartment blocks, contradicting the call; #1 is the W, a named five-star in a book that names no hotels; #3, #4, #8 are Sagrada and Batlló, both already printed. Typographic.

'4' names four charges, and no single frame shows them. Banknotes are the 'money exists' frame already killed (h-d03); Paral·lel platform (#3) and Plaça Nova (#6) are true but the 4 would not name them. Typographic.

'3' is the three anchors, and every candidate is the basilica alone: interiors (#4, #9) repeat the A04 square on the facing 2+1 poster (p37, one page later); exteriors (#1, #5, #7, #8) are the same subject; #2 is a sunset hilltop view (Bunkers p64 already holds the golden frame and that view); #3 and #6 are Sagrada over the city, which the Bunkers frame already shows. Typographic.
Every frame is Casa Batlló (façade, night, tiles, atrium), already printed as the Batlló square on the 2+1 poster; #2 is an unplaceable roofscape. One subject, one picture. Typographic.

The two true night terraces fail Clean: #2 has 'LA GAMBETA' on the awning bottom-left (exactly where the 20:30 is overprinted) and 'LLAMBER' on the umbrellas; #3 has a 'König' bar wordmark at centre and strangers' faces sharp at the tables. #4 is a neon wordmark, #5 an Italian 'Mercato di Mezzo' (contradicts the call), #8 a pintxos counter with an English 'Jalapeño and Cheese' card, #9 Batlló (printed). Typographic.

Not Barcelona (#1, #3, #4, #8, #9: India, a Christmas church, prayer crowds) or Sagrada Família again (#2, #5, #6, #7), already printed as the A04 interior square and seen from the Bunkers. Typographic.

The p52 close is about crowds and attention; the true frames are empty or half-empty metro platforms (#1 Paral·lel, #6), which show the opposite, and #4 has strangers' faces sharp, which the risk pages forbid. La Rambla from above is on p51, one page before. Typographic.

Mostly not Barcelona (#1 Australia, #4 Liverpool by Anfield, #5 an English village, #6, #9 South Asia). #3 is the Pont del Bisbe (true), but it has no tie to the failure modes, and as a lane it falls within 12 pages of the Poblenou 'lane' frame on p56. #8's 'Tourism kills the city' graffiti cannot be placed. Typographic.

Nothing that serves the Contract's prose: Camp Nou stands (#7, #8: Nike and Estrella wordmarks), a football pitch, generic façades. The true #1 (the Tres Xemeneies) and #6 (the Cathedral down a street) have no claim on p3, and #6 has a licence plate and a 'HOTEL' plate at its bottom corners.

The prose is about marks and a reading habit; no frame proves anything there. The true ones (Eixample aerial #1, which repeats A03 on p27; Park Güell #3, #5, the pavilions on the poster square; Arc de Triomf #8; Sagrada down an avenue #9) are views without a job. #7 has 'Barcelona Bus Turístic' branding.

The TMB 'M' sign (#1) and metro trains (#2, #4, #5, #9) are true, but the claim is that the airport ticket is not the one the metro card holds, and the p11 Zone 1 figure already makes it; #2 is FGC L7, the wrong network. Batlló (#3, #8) is printed; #7 is an FCB crest. Empty margin is not void here: Brunner's stack fills it.

The beach frames are good (#4 a gray Barceloneta, #5 the summer crush), but the chapter's beach is the timing closing on p21; a second Barceloneta two pages earlier breaks one subject, one picture. #1 repeats the Mapfre and Arts towers from p56; #2 is low sun; #6 and #9 are unplaceable streets.

place: Park Güell, Barcelona — the serpentine trencadís bench around the Nature Square terrace, in the ticketed monumental zone
how_known: Read at 2000×3000: the continuous undulating bench clad in broken-tile trencadís (glazed ochre and green capping, star and flower tiles, the raised seat bumps), the sand terrace floor, Aleppo pines below the balustrade — Gaudí and Jujol's bench, unique to Park Güell's terrace.
caption_proposed: Park Güell's serpentine bench on the terrace: the part your timed slot buys, and the free park does not.
subject_note: the curve of the tiled seat and backrest from the foreground to where it turns behind the trees
corners: TL: dark pine foliage; TR: tiled backrest and pines; BL: white trencadís seat front; BR: sandy terrace floor — no mark, text, logo or person
ai_signs: none — tile fragments irregular and grouted consistently, no repeats or melt
why: p23–24 say that the terrace, the viaducts and the monuments sit inside the ticketed zone and that no free route reaches them; this is the terrace, so it proves what the booking buys and why the free park is 'not a consolation prize' and not the same thing. Empty of people, so no faces. It is not the poster's Park Güell square (that is the entrance pavilions on Carrer d'Olot): different object, and 14 pages apart. keep_why if Ruth files a twice: the pavilions are the icon, the bench is the evidence. Printed whole at 264 px wide (4672 px native = 17.7×). Monument budget: this frame and A05 (p42), 19 pages apart.

La Rambla at eye level (#3, #6, #8) shows strangers' faces sharp on the pickpocket page, and the same street from above is already the plate on p51. Postcards (#1, a cliché), fruit (#2, price cards), Batlló (#9), the cable-car tower (#5) have no job here.

The Plan names no hill by name, so the Montjuïc cable car (#6) would need a claim the text does not make (and it carries the operator's lettering). The Cathedral (#8) has a 'COL…' hotel sign in the top-right corner; Tibidabo (#5 sunset, #7) is not in the book; Park Güell's tower (#1, #9) is the pavilion on the poster square; Sagrada (#2, #3 with a taxi's lettering) is printed. Poblenou closes the chapter two pages later anyway.
